head.citation-title: Studying the interfacial transition zone microstructure of pre-stressed high-strength concrete pipe piles
head.abstracts: © 2024The pre-stressed high-strength concrete (PHC) pipe piles are commonly applied for foundation reinforcement. The spun-cast method is employed to mold the PHC pipe piles, leading to the coarse aggregate assembling away from the internal surface of the piles and leaving a zone with less coarse aggregate. In this study, the region with assembling coarse aggregate was referred to as the concrete part, and the other region was called the mortar part. Autoclave curing is adopted to hasten the enhancement of PHC pipe pile strength. The main hydration product was replaced by tobermorite instead of CSH gel and CH was consumed mostly to react with finely ground quartz sand powder, under autoclave curing. The impact of these changes on the interfacial transition zone (ITZ) is worth attention. Therefore, this study focused on characterizing the microstructure of the ITZ. For the ITZ thickness of the concrete part and the mortar part, the nanoindentation was selected. Furthermore, BSE-image analysis is also utilized to examine the ITZ thickness, demonstrating the curve where changes in porosity fellows vary with the distance from the aggregate, and to compare the distribution of pore sizes between the ITZ and the paste. As deduced from analyzing nanoindentation results, BSE-images, and overestimating the ITZ thickness, the nanoindentation results are more suitable in the PHC pipe piles.

coredata.dc:description: The pre-stressed high-strength concrete (PHC) pipe piles are commonly applied for foundation reinforcement. The spun-cast method is employed to mold the PHC pipe piles, leading to the coarse aggregate assembling away from the internal surface of the piles and leaving a zone with less coarse aggregate. In this study, the region with assembling coarse aggregate was referred to as the concrete part, and the other region was called the mortar part. Autoclave curing is adopted to hasten the enhancement of PHC pipe pile strength. The main hydration product was replaced by tobermorite instead of CSH gel and CH was consumed mostly to react with finely ground quartz sand powder, under autoclave curing. The impact of these changes on the interfacial transition zone (ITZ) is worth attention. Therefore, this study focused on characterizing the microstructure of the ITZ. For the ITZ thickness of the concrete part and the mortar part, the nanoindentation was selected. Furthermore, BSE-image analysis is also utilized to examine the ITZ thickness, demonstrating the curve where changes in porosity fellows vary with the distance from the aggregate, and to compare the distribution of pore sizes between the ITZ and the paste. As deduced from analyzing nanoindentation results, BSE-images, and overestimating the ITZ thickness, the nanoindentation results are more suitable in the PHC pipe piles.
coredata.dc:title: Studying the interfacial transition zone microstructure of pre-stressed high-strength concrete pipe piles

mainterm.$: Thickness of the interfacial transition zone
